title: Grade 3 Science — Wed, Jun 25
description: Plants Around Us — Day 3 of 5: Leaves — shape, venation, functions
subject: science

questions.question: The thin lines visible on a leaf are called:
questions.explanation: The lines on a leaf are called veins. They carry water and minerals to all parts of the leaf and carry food away.

questions.question: In parallel venation, the veins are:
options: Running parallel (side by side) along the leaf
questions.explanation: Parallel venation means veins run side by side (parallel) from base to tip. Grasses, banana, rice and maize have parallel venation.

questions.question: Reticulate venation looks like:
options: A net or web pattern with branching veins
questions.explanation: Reticulate (net-like) venation has veins branching from a main central vein creating a net/web pattern. Most flowering plants — mango, rose, tulsi — have reticulate venation.

questions.question: Which plant shows PARALLEL venation?
questions.explanation: Maize (corn) has parallel venation — veins run side by side. Mango, peepal and rose all show reticulate venation.

questions.question: What is the main function of leaves?
questions.explanation: The primary function of leaves is photosynthesis — making food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide. Leaves are green because they contain chlorophyll.

questions.question: Transpiration is the process where leaves:
options: Release excess water as water vapour through tiny pores
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves through tiny pores called stomata. It cools the plant and helps in the movement of water up the stem.

questions.question: A banana leaf has veins running from base to tip in straight lines. What type of venation is this?
questions.explanation: Banana leaves have parallel venation — veins run side by side from the leaf base to the tip.

questions.question: Why are leaves flat and broad (in most plants)?
options: To maximize surface area for catching sunlight and absorbing CO₂
questions.explanation: Flat, broad leaves maximize the surface area exposed to sunlight and air, making photosynthesis more efficient. More surface = more light captured.

questions.question: A tulsi leaf has veins forming a net-like pattern. Which venation type is this?
questions.explanation: Tulsi has reticulate venation — a net-like branching pattern of veins, typical of most dicot flowering plants.

questions.question: Which statement about leaf functions is FALSE?
options: Leaves absorb water from the soil
Leaves take in CO₂ for photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Leaves do NOT absorb water from soil — that is the job of roots. Leaves absorb CO₂ from air, make food through photosynthesis and release water vapour through transpiration.

questions.question: Cactus has leaves modified into spines. Why?
options: To reduce water loss in dry desert conditions; the green stem does photosynthesis instead
Spines absorb water from the air
questions.explanation: In the desert, reducing water loss is crucial. Cactus leaves have become spines (minimal surface area = minimal transpiration). The green stem takes over photosynthesis.

questions.question: How does venation pattern relate to a plant's group?
options: It is random with no pattern
Parallel venation → monocot plants (like grasses); reticulate venation → dicot plants (like mango)
Both types occur randomly in all plants
questions.explanation: In plant classification: monocots (rice, wheat, maize) have parallel venation; dicots (mango, rose, tulsi) have reticulate venation. Venation type is a diagnostic feature.

questions.question: If you cover a leaf with black paper (blocking all light), what happens to that leaf?
options: It makes food faster in the dark
It cannot photosynthesize and will eventually yellow and die
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires light. Block light → no photosynthesis → no food for that leaf → it turns yellow (loses chlorophyll) and eventually dies.

questions.question: Leaves release oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis. Why is this important for animals and humans?
options: All living things need oxygen for respiration (breathing); without plants releasing oxygen, animals could not survive
Oxygen is used only by plants
questions.explanation: All animals (including humans) need oxygen to breathe and release energy. Plants produce oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis, making life on Earth possible.

questions.question: Leaves have tiny pores called stomata (mostly on the underside). Why on the UNDERSIDE?
options: The upper surface gets direct sunlight which would dry out stomata; the underside stays cooler
It is the same on both sides in all plants
questions.explanation: Stomata on the underside face away from direct sunlight. This reduces the drying-out effect (too much water loss) while still allowing gas exchange. It is an adaptation to conserve water.
